$comment: SHARED CONTRACT for outbound public-projection PII suppression.
Arkova has FOUR independent public, unauthenticated projections of the
same anchor rows, written in two languages:
1. SQL   — public.get_public_anchor(text) and its delegating sibling
public.get_public_anchor_by_fingerprint(text), both GRANTed to
`anon` and called straight from the browser over PostgREST by
the verify page, the embeddable widget, and the edge MCP tools.
2. TS    — services/worker/src/ctdl/ctdl-pii-guard.ts, behind
GET /api/v1/credentials/:publicId/ctdl.
3. TS    — services/worker/src/api/v1/verify.ts `buildVerificationResult`,
behind GET /api/v1/verify/:publicId, which router.ts allows
anonymously (`if (!req.apiKey && req.method === 'GET') next()`).
Also reached via oracle.ts and batch.ts, which reuse the same
builder.
4. TS    — services/worker/src/api/v1/provenance.ts, behind
GET /api/v1/verify/:publicId/provenance, mounted with NO
requireScope and NO auth middleware at all.
They drifted, and the drift IS the defect. It has now been found FOUR
times: the CTDL path was hardened (PR #1815) while the SQL path kept
shipping learner names and raw revocation reasons; then BOTH were hardened
while the verify path kept shipping `anchor.description` raw; then all
THREE were hardened while provenance kept shipping `revocation_reason` and
an X.509 Subject CN. A fifth (anchor-evidence.ts) is recorded as open under
known_ungated_projections. This file is the one place the rule is written
down, so no implementation can be changed alone — and, more to the point,
so the NEXT projection cannot be written without discovering the rule
already exists.
The TS value layer is ONE function, services/worker/src/api/v1/
public-projection-text.ts `publicFreeTextOrNull`, imported by every TS
projection. Do not copy it — a second copy is the drift in miniature.
Enforced by src/tests/public-anchor-pii-projection.contract.test.ts (static,
always runs), tests/rls/public-anchor-pii-projection.test.ts (live DB, runs
the vector corpus through the real anon-callable RPC), and two supertest
suites against the real anonymous Express routes:
services/worker/src/api/v1/verify-pii-projection.test.ts and
services/worker/src/api/v1/provenance-pii-projection.test.ts.
TO CHANGE THE RULE: edit this file, then ALL FOUR implementations, in ONE
PR. The tests fail otherwise — which is the entire point.
$ts_owner_note: ts_owner_module does not exist on main yet — it lands with PR #1815 (open,
out of draft). The contract test asserts its absence today and asserts full
parity the moment the file appears, so this arms itself with no follow-up
ticket. When #1815 merges, ts_owner_pending_pr becomes historical; leave it
as the record of why the self-arming branch exists.
DO NOT read this as 'the two implementations agree on main today'. They do
not. main's TS-side gate still lives in ts_pre_1815_module, and it is the
PRE-fix implementation that #1815 replaces. Measured divergences from this
contract, as of 2026-08-01:
- gates on DEGREE/CERTIFICATE only, AND requires a transcript keyword in
the free text; TRANSCRIPT is never gated by type. That is the bug #1815
fixes and the reason the SQL side could not simply copy it.
- no MAX_SCAN_CHARS; detectors run unbounded.
- 3 high-confidence families (email, SSN, phone), not 7.
- its SSN pattern makes separators OPTIONAL, so it fires on any bounded
9-digit run. The SQL side deliberately does not copy that: on a public
projection it would blank real fields containing an order number or a
numeric URL path segment.
The SQL detectors were verified vector-for-vector against #1815's guard, not
against ts_pre_1815_module. Parity with main becomes true when #1815 lands,
and the self-arming test starts enforcing it the same moment.
$unknown_type_note: SCRUM-3102 / migration 0390. An anchor with an ABSENT credential_type
(NULL, empty, or whitespace-only) is SUPPRESSED, exactly as an academic
record is — it is not treated as non-academic.
0385 keyed on `upper(COALESCE(p_credential_type,'')) IN (...)`, so an
untyped row evaluated to FALSE and took the PERMISSIVE branch, publishing
`filename` — the record's public display title and its schema.org `name`.
The seven detector families are all format- or keyword-anchored, so a bare
personal name passed. Measured in prod 2026-08-02: 24 of the 59 NULL-type
anchors (41%) carried a name-shaped filename, the densest such pocket in a
3,363,788-row corpus (academic types held 21; all other non-academic types
held 50, which is the accepted residual).
This is the `structural_keys` principle one level up: recognising danger
fails open, recognising SAFETY fails closed. The academic set recognises
safety by enumeration, so anything it cannot positively classify must be
suppressed.
A PRESENT non-academic type still publishes. `credential_type` is an enum
column, so a non-empty value is always a known type. Both implementations
must agree: SQL `is_academic_record_credential_type` (0390) and TS
`suppressesRecordFreeText` (ctdl-pii-guard.ts). Note the TS twin is a
SEPARATE function from `isEducationCredentialType`, which stays honest
about taxonomy and still returns false for null.
$academic_record_note: Records ABOUT AN IDENTIFIED LEARNER. These emit NO issuer- or
extraction-authored free text on either public projection.
CPE/CLE are deliberately EXCLUDED: practitioner records, not FERPA academic
records, and their descriptive title is the partner-facing value.
EVERY addition to this set silently replaces real credential titles with
$controlled_label_divergence: The CTDL serializer's academicRecordName() resolves a degree LEVEL from the
CTDL @type map ('Master Degree'). That map does not exist in the database,
so the SQL projection flattens DEGREE to 'Academic Degree'. TRANSCRIPT ->
'Academic Transcript' and CERTIFICATE -> 'Certificate' match the TS side
exactly. This divergence is DOCUMENTED, not silent — both labels are still
controlled vocabulary derived only from an enum, so neither can carry PII.
COPY SURFACE: these strings are USER-VISIBLE (the verify page renders
`filename` as the display title and embeds it in schema.org JSON-LD) but
they live in SQL, so `npm run lint:copy` cannot see them. If you widen this
map, check the new label against the CLAUDE.md §1.3 banned-terminology list
BY HAND — no linter covers this surface.
$ferpa_note: A THIRD education-type list lives in ferpa_module and deliberately DIFFERS:
it includes CLE. It drives the FERPA §99.33 re-disclosure NOTICE on the
verification API, not free-text suppression, and a continuing-legal-education
record is a practitioner record whose descriptive title is the partner-facing
value. Two lists with two purposes is fine. Two lists where nobody knows the
second exists is how this class of bug happens — so the contract test pins it,
and changing it is a decision rather than an accident.
CONFIRMED AS A DECISION, NOT AN ACCIDENT (verify-surface work): the same
list ALSO drives the §99.37 directory-information opt-out in verify.ts.
Both jobs are notice/consent mechanics over the wider practitioner+academic
set. Free-text suppression uses academic_record_credential_types instead.
ferpa.ts was deliberately NOT edited to reconcile the two.

known_ungated_projections.leaks: description and issuer_name, emitted raw at lines 254/256
known_ungated_projections.status: OPEN — not fixed by the verify or provenance work

$known_ungated_note: THIS LIST EXISTS SO THE CONTRACT CANNOT IMPLY COVERAGE IT DOES NOT HAVE.
Four projections are gated. At least one more anon-reachable projection of
the same rows is NOT. That is the recurring lesson, now observed FOUR
times: each pass gated the surface in front of it and missed the next.
`anchor-evidence.ts` is mounted `router.use('/anchor', anchorAnonAllow,
anchorEvidenceRouter)` in router.ts. `anchorAnonAllow` calls next() when the
method is GET/HEAD and there is NO api key, so an anonymous caller passes
straight through. `GET /:publicId/evidence` (line 326) then emits
`issuer_name: anchor.org_name` (254) and `description: anchor.description`
(256) verbatim — the same `description` field the verify projection gates.
Deliberately NOT fixed alongside provenance: it is its own public-API
surface with its own response contract, tests, and soak, and it is a
SIGNED EVIDENCE PACKAGE, so changing what it contains needs its own
decision about whether omission invalidates the package's own hash.
Delete this entry when it is gated.
The two sibling routers on that same `anchorAnonAllow` mount —
anchor-lifecycle.ts and anchor-extraction-manifest.ts — were checked and
emit no description/filename/issuer/revocation free text.
CHECKED AND NOT AFFECTED (do not re-audit from scratch):
- services/worker/src/api/v1/verify/attestation.ts — anon by design, but
emits no description/filename/revocation free text.
- services/worker/src/api/v1/attestations.ts — emits description and
filename, but every route self-guards with requireAuth/requireScope, so
it is not an anonymous projection.
- services/worker/src/api/v1/verify-proof.ts — merkle proof only, no free
text.
- services/worker/src/api/v1/anchor-lifecycle.ts,
services/worker/src/api/v1/anchor-extraction-manifest.ts — anon-reachable
via anchorAnonAllow, no free-text emission.
An earlier revision of this note listed only the /verify mounts as checked
while implying a complete sweep. It was not complete — the three /anchor
mounts had not been audited, which is how anchor-evidence.ts stayed
invisible. If you extend this list, say what you actually checked.
$provenance_note: GET /api/v1/verify/:publicId/provenance, mounted `router.use('/verify',
provenanceRouter)` with NO requireScope and NO auth middleware, and with no
auth check inside the module. Two leaks, needing two DIFFERENT treatments —
and the difference is the point.
1. `revocation_reason` is issuer-authored FREE TEXT that MIGHT carry
identity. Same two layers as everywhere else: academic records emit none
at all (matching 0385, which suppresses this exact field for those
types), every other type passes the value gate. Unconditional, not
gated on directory_info_opt_out, for the reason in $verify_note.
2. `signatures.signer_name` is a person's name BY CONSTRUCTION — it is set
from `cert.subject_cn` (signatures.ts:248), the X.509 Subject CN, beside
signer_org/location/contact_info. A value detector is USELESS here: the
measured finding behind this whole contract is that no regex separates a
bare name from an institution name. So it is never emitted, and it is
not even SELECTed, so a future edit to the detail string cannot
reintroduce it. This is the first field on any of these surfaces treated
as never-emit rather than gate-or-suppress, because it is the first that
is definitionally an identity rather than prose that may contain one.
WHAT SURVIVES: that a signature exists, when, its format and level, and
an `evidence_ref` (signatures.public_id) resolving the signer through an
AUTHENTICATED surface. If a verifier is entitled to the signer identity,
that entitlement is what should carry it — not an anonymous GET.
provenance_structural_fields are emitted unguarded and that is checked,
not assumed: `format` and `level` are DB CHECK-constrained closed
vocabularies (signatures_format_check: XAdES/PAdES/CAdES;
signatures_level_check: B-B/B-T/B-LT/B-LTA) AND Zod-enum validated at the
write path (signatures.ts:85). public_id and timestamp_token_id are
opaque identifiers.
THREE FACTS, THREE STRINGS. 'no reason provided' is a CLAIM. Asserting it
over a reason that exists but was suppressed would be false (§1.5, §1.13
R-7), so a suppressed reason degrades to a bare 'Revoked', which asserts
nothing about why. A genuinely absent reason keeps the original wording,
which is true. The contract test and the live suite pin all three.
$verify_note: GET /api/v1/verify/:publicId is the third projection and was the last to be
gated. `buildVerificationResult` emitted `anchor.description` RAW for every
credential type — including the three the other two projections suppress
outright — to an anonymous caller.
THE POLICY DECISION, stated rather than inherited. Suppression here is
UNCONDITIONAL, matching the other two, NOT conditional on
`directory_info_opt_out` as the surrounding REG-02 code is:
1. Opt-out means the DEFAULT IS PUBLISH, and default-publish is the defect
class. `anchors.directory_info_opt_out` defaults to false.
2. `description` was not covered by the opt-out anyway — REG-02 gates
issuer_name/recipient/dates and `description` was emitted underneath it,
so even an explicitly opted-out learner was exposed on this route.
3. One row, three anonymous projections, three answers is not a privacy
posture. The verify PAGE reads the SQL path, which suppresses; the API
disagreeing with the page it serves IS the drift.
The cost is real and bounded: an issuer-authored description no longer ships
on an academic record for anyone. It already does not ship on either other
public projection, so nothing publicly reachable elsewhere is lost.
DIVERGENCES FROM THE OTHER TWO, all deliberate:
- verify_fails_closed = false. The CTDL path 404s because its body is a
PUBLICATION; this body is a VERIFICATION ANSWER, so it omits the field
and still answers. Same reasoning as the SQL path (see 0385's
'OMISSION, NOT FAIL-CLOSED' block). Refusing would tell an anonymous
verifier a genuinely anchored document does not exist.
- verify_academic_suppressed_fields is ONE field, not five, because this
projection emits far less free text than the SQL one: there is no
`filename`, no metadata container, no revocation_reason on this schema.
`issuer_name` is value-gated but NOT structurally suppressed — the
issuer is an INSTITUTION, not the learner — which matches 0385 exactly.
- `jurisdiction` is value-gated, not suppressed: an informational
jurisdiction tag (§1.5) says nothing about the learner. Matches 0385.
- A DROPPED `issuer_name` is OMITTED here, where 0385 degrades it to the
literal 'Unknown Issuer'. Not an oversight. 0385 needs a non-NULL value
because its own fallback chain would otherwise fall through to
`o.display_name` — the ANCHORING org, frequently a different named
entity from the issuer — turning a redaction into a WRONG CLAIM about
who issued the credential (§1.5, §1.13 R-7). This projection has no
second source: `issuer_name` comes only from `organizations.display_name`
via `mapAnchorRow`, so omission cannot mis-attribute anything, and
`issuer_name` is already an optional key the response omits when the org
name is absent or the REG-02 opt-out fires. Emitting a literal
'Unknown Issuer' on a frozen API schema would INVENT a value where the
established contract is omit-when-absent.
verify_structural_api_rich_keys is an ALLOW-list and the gate FAILS CLOSED
against it: any STRING-valued API-RICH key not named there routes through
the value gate, so a future additive §1.8 field is gated by default rather
than shipping raw because nobody remembered. Same inversion as
$structural_keys_note. `sub_type` is bare `text` in the schema (no CHECK, no
enum) and `file_mime` is client-supplied, so both are gated; the numeric and
jsonb members carry no free text and pass through.
$fallback_label_note: The label a NON-academic record falls back to when its filename is dropped
by the value gate. Pinned here because it is a USER-VISIBLE string that
lives in SQL, so `npm run lint:copy` cannot see it and nothing else asserts
it. Check any replacement against the CLAUDE.md §1.3 banned-terminology list
$suppressed_vs_controlled: `filename` is the record's DISPLAY TITLE on the verify page and is embedded
in its schema.org JSON-LD, so it cannot be NULLed without breaking consumers
that assume a non-empty string — it takes a controlled label instead. It is
metadata.title and metadata.credential_title are OMITTED rather than given
the label. Emitting it there would leave the `metadata` object non-empty
after jsonb_strip_nulls, which flips the verify card out of its 'no metadata'
render mode into the key-value list — where neither key is hidden — and the
card would read 'Title: Academic Degree' and 'Credential Title: Academic
Degree' beneath a type banner that already says 'Academic Degree'. Omitting
preserves the existing render shape and states the label exactly once.
$ungated_keys_note: Keys the projection emits WITHOUT a value gate and WITHOUT being structural.
Empty is the goal. The contract test DERIVES the actual set from the latest
migration that redefines get_public_anchor and fails if it differs from this
list — so per-field wrapping, which is opt-in and therefore ungated by
default, becomes a reviewed decision instead of an accident. Adding a key
here requires stating why it is safe.
$projection_keys_note: EVERY `'key', <expr>` pair the contract test must find in the latest
redefiner of get_public_anchor. Pinned because the derived gate is only as
honest as its parse: an empty 'ungated' result means BOTH 'everything is
gated' AND 'the matcher stopped matching', and those must not be
indistinguishable. Set equality here makes a parse that silently stops
seeing keys fail LOUDLY instead of reporting a clean bill of health.
Adding a key to the projection therefore requires adding it here — which is
the point: a new public key is a reviewed decision. Classify it as
structural_keys (no cleaner needed) or leave it out of that list, in which
case it MUST route through a cleaner.
`recipient` and `recipient_identifier` are absent on purpose. Neither is a
projected free-text key: the first is the raw SELECT input consumed by the
keyed HMAC, the second is that HMAC's output. Both are asserted by the
dedicated 'keeps the recipient identifier a KEYED HMAC' test.
$structural_keys_note: The ONLY keys exempt from the cleaner requirement: verification-bearing or
structural values that carry no issuer- or extraction-authored free text —
facts (bitcoin_block, network_receipt_id), sizes, the derived record_uri,
opaque identifiers (public_id, issuer_public_id, fingerprint), the literal
NULL merkle_proof_hash, and the three container keys whose CHILDREN are
each gated in their own right (metadata, cpe_metadata, cle_metadata).
This list is an ALLOW-list and the gate FAILS CLOSED against it: any key
not named here must call a cleaner. The earlier design was the inverse — it
tried to RECOGNISE anchor-controlled expressions and skipped everything it
did not recognise, so it was blind to the `g.safe_metadata ->> '...'` alias
that 0385 itself introduced, and to every source expression a future
migration might invent. Recognising danger fails open; recognising safety
$url_note: Emitted URLs (proof_url, source_url, registry_url) go through a URL-specific
cleaner that DROPS on overflow instead of truncating. Truncating a URL
produces a valid-looking WRONG link that the frontend renders as a live
anchor — strictly worse than omitting the field. Query string and fragment
are stripped BEFORE the PII scan: structural, not heuristic, since a query
parameter is the carrier an identifier rides in on.
$learner_name_divergence: The CTDL serializer carries two capitalised-pair name patterns for
field-level suppression. The SQL projection deliberately does NOT implement
them. Measured, not assumed:
TRUE POSITIVES: zero. Run against this file's own leak_vectors, both
patterns return false for every single one — bare, all-caps, non-ASCII,
record-noun-first, apostrophe, hyphenated. `[A-Z][a-z]{1,}` cannot express
those shapes. Both implementations agree on this; it is the empirical
confirmation of PR #1815's own finding.
FALSE POSITIVES: abundant, because `for` is a bare preposition. 'Center
for Professional Development', 'Society for Human Resource Management',
'Institute for Supply Management', 'Ethics for Trial Lawyers', 'Credit for
Prior Learning', 'Revoked for Non Payment' — all dropped. The second
pattern takes ordinary titles the same way: 'Data Science degree',
'Project Management certificate'.
A detector with zero measured true positives and abundant measured false
positives has negative value, and the cost is higher here than on the CTDL
path: these fields are the verify page's PRIMARY DISPLAY (`filename` is the
record title and its schema.org `name`), not optional JSON-LD properties.
Learner names ARE covered on this path, structurally — an academic record
emits no issuer- or extraction-authored free text at all, which is
precision-independent and catches every shape above.
The false-positive strings are pinned in must_publish_vectors, so
reintroducing the patterns fails the suite rather than silently blanking
real credentials.
$detector_note: High-confidence detectors are FORMAT- or KEYWORD-anchored, run on every
credential type, and are the only ones precise enough to act on alone.
